sources.title: Setting Up a K3s Kubernetes Cluster on NVIDIA DGX Spark with Full GPU Support
sources.summary: Walkthrough for installing k3s with Docker as the container runtime on DGX Spark, then adding the NVIDIA GPU Operator via helm with driver/toolkit disabled since DGX OS ships them preinstalled.

facts.claim: Docker runtime is set as default nvidia via `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker --set-as-default` then `sudo systemctl restart docker`
k3s install command used: `curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -s - --docker --write-kubeconfig-mode 644 --disable traefik`

GPU Operator installed via `helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator --namespace gpu-operator --create-namespace --set driver.enabled=false --set toolkit.enabled=false --wait` because DGX Spark drivers/toolkit are pre-installed
GPU capacity verified with `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[].status.capacity'` looking for "nvidia.com/gpu": "1"
This guide uses k3s with Docker as the container runtime, not containerd

sources.relevance_to_us: This is the base recipe we'd start from for k3d/k3s-with-GPU on our incoming NvidiaSpark-1, though it uses Docker runtime rather than containerd (the second Collabnix article gives the containerd path we'd more likely use with k3d/k3s default containerd).

sources.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark + Kubernetes: Run GPU Workloads on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip
sources.summary: More detailed containerd-based k3s+GPU-Operator recipe for GB10, including the critical unified-memory device-plugin fix (v0.17.4+), time-slicing config, and a troubleshooting table.

facts.claim: GB10's unified memory makes the classic device plugin crash because nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo returns "Not Supported"; fix is device plugin version >= v0.17.4
facts.evidence: Critical Fix: Unified Memory Architecture (UMA) section

facts.claim: Hardware baseline cited: GB10 chip, 128 GB LPDDR5x unified (arm64), driver 580.95.05 (CUDA 12.x), K8s K3s v1.30+, device plugin v0.17.4+
containerd runtime configured via `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=containerd --config=/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/etc/containerd/config.toml.tmpl --set-as-default`
GPU Operator installed with `--set devicePlugin.version=v0.17.4` alongside driver.enabled=false and toolkit.enabled=false

Time-slicing ConfigMap example exposes 1 physical GPU as 4 schedulable slices via `sharing.timeSlicing.resources` with replicas: 4, applied and then `kubectl patch clusterpolicy/cluster-policy -n gpu-operator --type merge -p '{"spec":{"devicePlugin":{"config":{"name":"time-slicing-config","default":"any"}}}}'`
"Memory-Usage: Not Supported" in nvidia-smi is expected/benign on unified-memory iGPU; per-process GPU memory still shows, only the aggregate field is blank
MIG is unavailable on GB10 -- time-slicing is the only GPU-sharing mechanism (no hard memory isolation, temporal sharing only)

Troubleshooting table: "error getting device memory: Not Supported" -> old device plugin, fix use v0.17.4+; node shows 0 GPU capacity -> plugin crashed, check `kubectl logs -n gpu-operator -l app=nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset`; pods stuck Pending -> apply time-slicing config; CUDA OOM -> lower --gpu-memory-utilization to 0.8

sources.relevance_to_us: This is the single most load-bearing source for ch8/ch9 -- gives the exact device-plugin version floor and the UMA memory-reporting quirk we need to document so ch9's CSO-operator-on-aarch64 chapter doesn't misread 'Not Supported' as a broken cluster.

sources.title: Docker Compose vs Kubernetes on NVIDIA DGX Spark: Which Setup Should You Choose for NIM Microservices?
sources.summary: Decision framework comparing docker-compose and k3s Kubernetes for running NVIDIA NIM microservices on a single vs multi-node DGX Spark deployment.

facts.claim: Docker Compose deploys in roughly 10 minutes vs roughly 30 minutes for Kubernetes (K3s) on DGX Spark, per the article's own estimate
GPU performance of NIM containers is described as identical between compose and k8s -- difference is only in orchestration overhead
Recommendation: choose Kubernetes when managing two or more Spark nodes needing production-grade scheduling; choose docker-compose for single-node dev/prototyping
Both setups reportedly use port 8000 for the NIM HTTP API and demonstrate with Llama 3.1 8B Instruct

sources.relevance_to_us: Useful for ch5 (NIM on Spark parity) and ch8's framing of when k3d/k8s is even worth it on a single-node Spark before we scale to multi-Spark (ch22).

sources.title: Local Kubernetes Cluster with K3s on Nvidia DGX Spark
sources.summary: NVIDIA developer forum thread (Dec 2025) where user shahizat posted a working k3s+GPU recipe for serving Qwen3-4B via vLLM on DGX Spark; community follow-ups suggested Talos Linux as an alternative and reported a working network-operator based multi-node setup.

facts.claim: User shahizat's guide (dated Dec 26, 2025) modified /etc/docker/daemon.json to set NVIDIA Container Runtime as default, restarted Docker, then ran `curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | INSTALL_K3S_EXEC="--docker --write-kubeconfig-mode 644 --disable=traefik" sh -`
Deployment manifests included a 50GB PVC, a Secret for Hugging Face token, a Deployment requesting `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`, and a Service on port 8000; pod reached Running after 38 minutes
Commenter justin.garrison (Dec 27, 2025) suggested Talos Linux 1.12 with an optimized 6.18 kernel as an alternative Kubernetes-first OS approach for DGX Spark
Commenter sakshamconsul later reported implementing the network-operator for multi-node GPU+RDMA configs and published a reference repo

sources.relevance_to_us: Confirms the k3s+Docker-runtime path is community-validated on real GB10 hardware, and flags Talos Linux as a documented alternative worth a footnote in ch2/ch9.

sources.title: Invalid Runtime Name: nvidia
sources.summary: NVIDIA developer forum thread confirming this Docker GPU-runtime error occurs on DGX Spark/GB10 ARM64; root cause is the preinstalled nvidia-container-toolkit not being configured for Docker, fixed by `nvidia-ctk runtime configure`.

facts.claim: User AndrewMyers reported (Nov 8, 2025) `docker: Error response from daemon: unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia` on DGX Spark/GB10 ARM64 despite nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18.0-1 being installed
Moderator aniculescu (Dec 10, 2025) said root cause was that the toolkit came preinstalled on DGX Spark but wasn't fully configured for user access, not a buildkit corruption issue
Fix: run `nvidia-ctk runtime configure`, which generates /etc/docker/daemon.json with a `runtimes.nvidia` entry (path nvidia-container-runtime), then `service docker restart`
A follow-up clarification (Dec 11, 2025) noted `--gpus=all` alone may be sufficient on DGX Spark without explicitly specifying the nvidia runtime

sources.relevance_to_us: First failure mode to check in ch2/ch8's day-1 setup runbook if a fresh DGX Spark's docker GPU test fails before we even get to k3s/k3d.

sources.title: Bug: Embedded k3s in OpenShell gateway fails on DGX Spark GB10 (ARM64, Ubuntu 24.04, cgroup v2)
sources.summary: Report of an embedded k3s instance (inside a different product's gateway container, OpenShell/NemoClaw) failing to initialize on DGX Spark GB10 due to cgroup v2 kubelet errors, even though standalone GPU workloads on the same host work fine.

facts.claim: System pods get stuck CrashLoopBackOff/Pending with kubelet error "Failed to kill all the processes attached to cgroup" err='os: process not initialized' on DGX Spark GB10, ARM64 Ubuntu 24.04, cgroup v2
The failure is isolated to k3s orchestration -- standalone GPU workloads (a ~70GB Nemotron vLLM) run fine on the same host, confirming GPU/network infra itself is not the problem
Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Docker 28.x, cgroup v2, OpenShell CLI 0.0.7-0.0.13; issue persisted despite setting Docker's default-cgroupns-mode to "host"
facts.evidence: Key Technical Details / Direct DGX Spark Relevance sections

sources.relevance_to_us: A cautionary data point for ch8: cgroup v2 + embedded/nested k3s on GB10 can hit kubelet-level cgroup failures unrelated to GPU access itself -- worth a troubleshooting note if we ever nest k3d/k3s inside another container runtime on the Spark.

sources.title: dgx-spark-vllm-k8s
sources.summary: Production-oriented repo deploying DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a two-node DGX Spark K3s cluster with tensor parallelism, NCCL-over-RDMA, and detailed UMA memory-limit tuning for vLLM.

facts.claim: Two GB10 nodes (spark-0 control-plane+head, spark-1 worker) run vLLM with tensor-parallel-size 2 over NCCL/RoCEv2 RDMA on a direct 200GbE QSFP link (eth2, 192.168.74.0/30)
Container `resources.limits.memory` caps GPU allocations too on UMA; of ~119.67 GiB nvidia-smi reports, ~24-29 GiB is CUDA driver/hardware reserved, leaving ~90-95 GiB effective CUDA-usable memory
facts.evidence: Critical Hardware Detail: UMA Memory Architecture section

facts.claim: Working container memory limit found empirically: 85 GiB too low (OOM-killed during model load), 93 GiB stable, 95 GiB too high (can't schedule, exceeds node allocatable)
Infra prerequisites table: K3s v1.32+ or Talos Linux, Cilium CNI >=1.18 (native routing), Multus (Siderolabs install-cni), Spiderpool 1.2.x, GPU Operator v26.3.2
vLLM crash leaves ~31 GiB in leaked CUDA contexts per cycle; after 3-4 crash-loops free memory drops below required threshold; fix is `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0` on startup
facts.evidence: Critical Production Fixes: GPU Reset section

facts.claim: Worker pods must run with NO liveness/readiness probes in --headless mode, since probe failures on the headless worker kill the pod and hang NCCL for the head
Decode throughput measured at ~17-42 tokens/second (varies by context size) at 0.75 GPU memory utilization, 1M context, 2 concurrent sequences, fp8 KV cache; time-to-first-token ~6.3s at 32K input

sources.relevance_to_us: The most concrete real-world multi-node GB10 Kubernetes GPU-memory-limit tuning example we found -- directly useful for ch6 (concurrency/GPU memory) and ch22 (multi-Spark scale-out) as well as ch9's UMA guidance; the exact GiB thresholds are worth citing verbatim.

sources.title: dgxarley
sources.summary: Ansible-driven, experimental/dev-labeled repo standing up a heterogeneous K3s cluster (x86_64 control plane + 4x DGX Spark ARM64 compute nodes) for distributed SGLang inference, with detailed Multus/CNI-path and NVIDIA device-plugin mount gotchas specific to K3s.

facts.claim: Cluster is 1 control plane (HP EliteDesk 800 G4, x86_64) + 4 DGX Spark ARM64 compute nodes connected via QSFP mesh, running SGLang pipeline-parallel serving of nvidia/MiniMax-M2.5-NVFP4 by default

K3s stores CNI plugin configs at /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/etc/cni/net.d rather than the standard /etc/cni/net.d, requiring the Multus daemon container to mount the parent /var/lib/rancher/k3s/data so symlink targets resolve

NVIDIA device plugin needs a hostPath mount of /driver-root for NVML library discovery -- missing it causes silent fallback to CPU-based device resolution; CDI spec generation needs a writable /var/run/cdi mount, not read-only /etc/cdi
Time-slicing default is 4 replicas per physical GPU in this repo's device-plugin config
facts.evidence: GPU-Specific Technical Notes point 1 / Time-slicing trade-off

facts.claim: Measured NCCL bus bandwidth: 9.78 GB/s over RoCE vs 2.12 GB/s over TCP socket transport (4.6x speedup), requiring SR-IOV VFs, host-side IPv4 config, and privileged pod access to RDMA hardware
Project explicitly marked "development/experimental", provided as-is, not warrantied for production

sources.relevance_to_us: Concrete K3s+Multus+device-plugin mount gotchas (driver-root hostPath, CNI path under /var/lib/rancher/k3s) that would bite us if we ever multi-node beyond a single NvidiaSpark-1; flag as experimental-tier evidence, not a vetted recipe.

sources.title: k3d docs: Using GPUs / CUDA
sources.summary: Official k3d documentation on enabling CUDA/GPU support: requires building a custom k3s node image on a non-Alpine (CUDA) base because the NVIDIA container runtime isn't supported on Alpine, plus explicit RuntimeClass and per-pod runtimeClassName usage.

facts.claim: CUDA workloads require the NVIDIA Container Runtime and containerd must be configured to use it; the native k3s image is Alpine-based and "the NVIDIA container runtime is not supported on Alpine yet"
facts.evidence: Prerequisites / Why a Custom Image is Needed sections

facts.claim: The documented fix is a custom Dockerfile that swaps the base to something like nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04, installs the container toolkit, runs `nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=containerd`, copies in the k3s binaries, and bundles the NVIDIA device plugin daemonset manifest at /var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests/
You must explicitly add `runtimeClassName: nvidia` to every Pod spec that needs the GPU (a RuntimeClass with the nvidia handler must also be defined)

Cluster launched with the custom image via `k3d cluster create gputest --image=$IMAGE --gpus=1`; the doc does not specify which GPU architectures/models are supported, only that the NVIDIA Container Toolkit must be on the host

sources.relevance_to_us: This is the general k3d-CUDA recipe (not GB10-specific); no source we found documents anyone actually running k3d (as opposed to plain k3s) on a real DGX Spark -- open question for ch8/ch9 whether the Alpine-base swap is even needed given DGX OS already runs an Ubuntu-based host with containerd, or whether k3d's Docker-in-Docker layer adds friction on unified memory.

sources.title: NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin releases
sources.summary: Release notes page for the NVIDIA Kubernetes device plugin; the model's extraction found v0.17.4 (Sept 9, 2024) noted as "Ignore errors getting device memory using NVML" -- the closest documented tie to the UMA nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo issue, and v0.18.0 changing GPU memory units from MB to MiB.

facts.claim: v0.17.4 release notes include the line "Ignore errors getting device memory using NVML"
facts.evidence: v0.17.4 entry, per fetched release notes

facts.claim: v0.18.0 release notes include "Use MiB instead of MB for gpu-memory"
facts.evidence: v0.18.0 entry, per fetched release notes

facts.claim: The fetched release notes contain no explicit mention of GB10, DGX Spark, or ARM64/aarch64 by name in the versions checked (v0.17.3, v0.17.4, v0.18.0)

sources.relevance_to_us: Confirms the Collabnix article's "v0.17.4 fixes UMA memory errors" claim maps to a real release note ("Ignore errors getting device memory using NVML") even though NVIDIA's own notes don't name GB10/DGX Spark explicitly -- worth citing both together in ch9 rather than either alone. Caveat: this was a fetch-tool summarization of the releases page, not a raw diff -- verify the exact v0.17.4 changelog text directly before quoting it in the guide.

sources.title: K3s docs: NVIDIA Container Runtime Support (Advanced)
sources.summary: Official k3s documentation section on NVIDIA runtime support: install nvidia-container-runtime packages, then install/restart k3s, which auto-detects and wires in the NVIDIA runtime to containerd's config.toml -- no manual config.toml.tmpl edits required in the base case.

facts.claim: Steps: follow https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/ to add the nvidia-container repo, install packages such as nvidia-container-runtime, cuda-drivers-fabricmanager-515, nvidia-headless-515-server, then install or restart k3s

K3s automatically adds NVIDIA runtimes to the containerd configuration depending on what runtime executables are found on the host -- no custom config.toml.tmpl is required in the documented base case
facts.evidence: Key Points / No Custom config.toml.tmpl Required sections

facts.claim: Detection can be verified with `grep nvidia /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/etc/containerd/config.toml`
If NVIDIA runtime is not set as the containerd default, pods must set `runtimeClassName: nvidia` (a built-in RuntimeClass k3s ships)
facts.evidence: Pod specification requirement / RuntimeClass available bullets

sources.relevance_to_us: The canonical, version-agnostic k3s+NVIDIA baseline; note it contradicts nothing in the Collabnix guides but is simpler -- k3s can auto-detect the runtime without the explicit `nvidia-ctk runtime configure --config=.../config.toml.tmpl` step some blog guides show, worth testing both paths on the real NvidiaSpark-1 for ch8.

open_questions: No source found documents anyone actually running k3d (as opposed to plain k3s) directly on a real DGX Spark GB10 -- the k3d-CUDA doc is generic guidance only. Confirm on our own NvidiaSpark-1 whether k3d's Docker-in-Docker node containers even need the Alpine-base swap, given DGX OS's host is already Ubuntu/containerd-based.

NVIDIA's own k8s-device-plugin release-notes text for v0.17.4 was retrieved via a fetch-tool summarization rather than the raw page/changelog diff -- re-verify the exact wording ("Ignore errors getting device memory using NVML") directly against https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin/releases/tag/v0.17.4 before quoting it as a direct citation.

GPU Operator version to standardize on is unclear: Collabnix's guide passes --set devicePlugin.version=v0.17.4 explicitly; dgx-spark-vllm-k8s's prerequisites table cites GPU Operator v26.3.2 as a whole-chart version. These are two different version namespaces (device-plugin sub-component vs whole operator chart) and need reconciling before ch9 picks one pinned recipe.

Whether k3s should run with --docker (Docker runtime, as most guides here use) or plain containerd (k3s's default) on our actual NvidiaSpark-1 is unresolved -- both paths appear in different sources; pick one during day-1 setup (ch2/ch8) and document why.

The NemoClaw #878 cgroup-v2 kubelet failure is on an embedded/nested k3s inside a different product's gateway container, not a bare k3s install -- unclear whether this risk applies to a straightforward k3s/k3d install on the bare DGX OS host; worth a quick smoke test rather than assuming it will recur.

load_bearing_claims.claim: GB10's unified memory makes the classic NVIDIA device plugin fail on nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo ("Not Supported"), and the fix is device plugin version v0.17.4 or newer.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: This is the single gating fact for whether GPU pods even schedule on a GB10 k8s node -- getting the device-plugin version wrong means `nvidia.com/gpu` capacity never appears and every GPU workload in ch9-ch11 silently stays Pending. Must be verified directly against the real device-plugin changelog and tested on our own NvidiaSpark-1 before it goes in the guide as fact rather than blog claim.

load_bearing_claims.claim: On DGX Spark UMA, container resources.limits.memory caps GPU allocation too -- effective CUDA-usable memory is roughly 90-95 GiB out of the ~119.67 GiB nvidia-smi reports, with ~93 GiB found as the stable working container memory limit for a large model.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Directly determines how ch6 (concurrency/GPU memory) and ch9 size pod memory requests/limits for any GPU workload on the Spark -- getting this wrong causes either OOM-kills or unschedulable pods, and this is the only source with concrete measured GiB thresholds rather than a general statement.

load_bearing_claims.claim: MIG is unavailable on GB10; time-slicing (temporal sharing only, no hard memory isolation) is the only GPU-sharing mechanism available in Kubernetes on the Spark.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Sets the ceiling on multi-tenant GPU sharing strategy for ch8/ch9 -- if we plan any multi-workload GPU isolation story for the guide, MIG is off the table and we must design around time-slicing's lack of memory isolation, which changes how safely we can co-locate NiFi/Flink GPU workloads with LLM inference on the same Spark node.
